title: OpenSSL QUIC peer can exhaust memory with RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames
why: OpenSSL rates it Low: a malicious QUIC peer can make an app that uses OpenSSL's own QUIC code run out of memory. It's a crash, not code execution, there's no exploit or reported attack, and it isn't on CISA KEV. GitHub's advisory database shows 9.1; that score isn't OpenSSL's or CISA's (CISA scored it 7.5).
page_if: public exploit code or reported attacks, or a CISA KEV listing
a widely used server or client is shown to be exposed through OpenSSL's QUIC stack

facts.text: OpenSSL's advisory (24 Nov 2026, Low): the QUIC stack queues a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame for every retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame with no limit, so a malicious QUIC peer can cause an out-of-memory denial of service. It's an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-84784.
Affected: OpenSSL 4.1, 4.0 and 3.5. Not affected: 3.0, 1.1.1 and 1.0.2. OpenSSL didn't analyse 3.1 to 3.4 or 3.6, which are out of support. The FIPS module isn't affected.
No fixed release yet: 4.1.1, 4.0.4 and 3.5.10 are scheduled for 1 Dec 2026; the newest release is 4.1.0 (23 Oct). The fix is in the public repository.

Scores differ: CISA's entry on the CVE record gives 7.5 (availability only) and SSVC "Exploitation: none"; GitHub's advisory database gives 9.1 (confidentiality and availability high). NVD hasn't analysed it. Not on CISA KEV (catalog of 23 Nov).

sources.title: OpenSSL: security advisory, Low, fixes due 1 Dec
CVE record: CVE-2026-107494, affected versions, CISA 7.5

history.text: Evaluated: watch, no page. Low-rated denial of service in OpenSSL's QUIC code; GitHub shows 9.1, CISA's score is 7.5. The same advisory has a second Low QUIC memory bug, CVE-2026-84785, not tracked separately.
